summary: Laclede County steel lookout, 100 ft, described by a 1939 survey and named in a 1937 newspaper report; the lookout page marks it removed with no date.

facts.design: Steel structure with a glass-enclosed observation platform
facts.status_note: The lookout history page marks the tower Removed, with no date or method given.

events.note: Houston Herald report of January 28, 1937, quoted on the Gulf page, names the Lynchburg tower with the Roby tower as towers that observed parts of the Roubidoux District. No build date is given.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description of 1939 describes the Lynchburg lookout tower as a steel structure 100 feet high with a glass-enclosed observation platform on top.

evidence.supports: Lynchburg: Laclede County, Mark Twain National Forest, township and range 32N-13W-13
evidence.quote: Missouri Lookouts - Laclede County - Mark Twain National Forest - 32N-13W-13

evidence.supports: 1939 survey station description, steel tower 100 feet high with glass-enclosed platform
evidence.quote: LYNCHBURG LOOKOUT TOWER, A STEEL STRUCTURE 100 FEET HIGH WITH A GLASS-ENCLOSED OBSERVATION PLATFORM ON TOP.

evidence.supports: Survey station described by the Coast and Geodetic Survey in 1939
evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1939 (FBQ)

evidence.supports: Status on the lookout page: removed
The Houston Herald report is dated January 28, 1937
The 1937 report names the Roby and Lynchburg towers as observing parts of the District
evidence.quote: practically all areas of the District not observed by the Roby and Lynchburg towers, can be clearly seen.

evidence.supports: The 1937 report describes a 100-foot steel tower built by a Lynchburg CCC crew for the Roubidoux District of the Gardner National Forest, which is the Gulf tower
evidence.quote: a crew of boys from the Lynchburg CCC Camp have just completed the erection of the third all-steel, 100-foot fire lookout tower to be built in the Roubidoux District of the Gardner National Forest.

evidence.supports: Mark Twain National Forest was established in 1939

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1937 report places the Roubidoux District in the Gardner National Forest, while the lookout page and the brief name the Mark Twain National Forest, established in 1939. No source read explains how the two names relate, so the record keeps Mark Twain National Forest and the story reports both names.

sources.title: Gulf - Forest Lookouts (quotes the Houston Herald, January 28, 1937)

notes_for_editor: One 1939 federal survey description (quoted on the lookout page) and one 1937 newspaper report (quoted on the Gulf page). No builder, build date, staffing, or removal date was found. The 1937 Lynchburg CCC crew built the Gulf tower, not this one; the story says so. The 1937 report uses the Gardner National Forest name for the Roubidoux District; the page and brief use Mark Twain National Forest (see resolved_conflicts). Wikipedia gives September 23, 1939 in its infobox and September 11, 1939 in its text for the forest; the story uses the year only. Height 30.5 m is 100 ft converted; the survey figure is the only height source.
